- **4 am Màrt 2009 DE** — *An Taigh-òsta Grianach* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). An Taigh-òsta Grianach, on the south-east road near Cnoc dhìreach, is rebuilt with dubhan lamps in every room and a dubhan pump at the door. It is the first inn on the island to sell fuel as well as beds.
- **2 an Giblean 2009 DE** — *The ore engines laid up* (Muileann chrom). The Rail Board's ore-fired engines are laid up in a siding at Muileann chrom and never run again. The yard families who drove them are retrained on the dubhan engines, those who will be.
- **11 an t-Sultain 2009 DE** — *An Taigh-seinnse Reòta* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the north road above Muileann fhada is the last of the great inns to keep a wick lamp in every room. Its landlord writes to the Board that the dubhan smell drives away his guests. It does not, and he puts in the lamps the following year.
- **10 an Dàmhair 2009 DE** — *Muileann dhearg closed* (Muileann dhearg). The last working face under Muileann dhearg is closed. The town's remaining families are moved by the Board to Seann Toll on the coast, and Muileann dhearg is left with its chapel, its graves and a caretaker.
- **27 an t-Iuchar 2010 DE** — *The Muileann dhearg families at Seann Toll* (Seann Toll). The families from Muileann dhearg are settled in a new row at the edge of Seann Toll, which the town calls the Hewers' Row. Few of them find work at sea. Most work on the dubhan tanks at the harbour.
- **25 an Lùnastal 2010 DE** — *Muileann dhearg's chapel* (Muileann dhearg). The Fèidh chapel at Muileann dhearg is given to the town's caretaker to keep, with the graves. The Fèidh school at Caol shean sends a teacher once a year to hold the town's one remaining lecture, which few come to.
- **23 an t-Sultain 2010 DE** — *The word spreads before the fuel does*. "Dubhan" begins appearing in common speech to mean the fuel itself, not the man, years before the economy built on it is complete.
- **22 an Dàmhair 2010 DE** — *Dubhan-tùsail* (Caol shean). The word 'dubhan-tùsail' is first recorded, in a letter of the Fèidh school at Caol shean, for an early attempt at anything that looked like a dead end before it wasn't. The letter uses it of the school's own revival.
- **1 an Cèitean 2011 DE** — *The Rail Board's new name* (Muileann chrom). The Rail Board drops 'ore' from the name of its main line in its own timetables, calling it only the line. Everyone else goes on calling it the ore line.
- **30 an Cèitean 2011 DE** — *The Guild of Hewers dissolved* (Achadh dhomhain). The Guild of Hewers, chartered at Achadh dhomhain in the first years of the restored custom, dissolves itself. Its rolls, its oath-stone of ore and its sick-roll go to the library. Its last master, Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh, writes that the guild had outlived the mountain's patience.
- **28 an t-Ògmhios 2011 DE** — *The bath-house given to the Rite* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The bath-house at the hot springs near Muileann ruadh, built by the Hewers for their sick, passes to the Rite's custodians with the guild's other goods. It is opened to anyone who pays, the first time it has been open to Tuathaich.
- **1 am Màrt 2012 DE** — *The Achadh dhomhain hall* (Achadh dhomhain). The Hewers' hall at Achadh dhomhain, sold before the guild dissolved, becomes a dubhan depot. Its carved lintel, with the guild's oath cut into it, is left in place over the pumps.
- **9 am Màrt 2012 DE** — *The dubhan economy takes shape*. Markets, military logistics, and shipping begin shifting wholesale to the new fuel. The obsidian caste, watching its own power source fail, does not object.
- **4 an t-Sultain 2012 DE** — *The house of Mac Ùisdein moves* (Ros dhomhain). The house of Mac Ùisdein sells what remains of its share in the Sloc Mòr's spoil and quarry and puts its money into dubhan shipping at Ros dhomhain. Of the families that held the vein, it is the only one that moved before the vein failed it.
- **15 an t-Sultain 2012 DE** — *The fleet's first dubhan hulls* (Ros dhomhain). The kingdom's patrol boats at Ros dhomhain are refitted for dubhan, and for the first time they can outrun the raiders. The next two raider hulks taken are brought into Ros dhomhain under tow.
- **2 an t-Iuchar 2013 DE** — *Raiders taken to Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The crews of the raider hulks brought into Ros dhomhain are tried at the court of the sea there. Several of them are Tuathaich. The court hangs none, sends the Ròdaich among them to the quarries at Achadh dhomhain and the Tuathaich home to the north.
- **29 an Lùnastal 2013 DE** — *The Fuel-Fitters chartered* (Seann Skell). The fitters of dubhan engines, who had worked outside every guild, are chartered as the Guild of Fuel-Fitters at Seann Skell on the southern coast. Its rolls, like those of every guild before it, are open to Ròdaich only. The Tuathaich fitters already in the trade are let go.
- **27 an t-Sultain 2013 DE** — *Tuathaich fitters go north* (Caol mhòr). The fitters let go by the charter rule go back to the northern towns and fit engines there without a guild. Caol mhòr's harbour has more dubhan boats than any port of its size in the south within a few years.
- **24 an t-Samhain 2013 DE** — *The Moot on the new economy* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr, under Martha Greaves, debates whether the north should take up the new fuel or keep to its own seams. The Moot votes to take it up. The delegates from the western pit towns walk out.
- **8 am Màrt 2014 DE** — *The Tuathaich depots* (Ceann mhòr). Dubhan depots open at Caol mhòr, Doire ghlas and Ceann mhòr, supplied by sea. Martha Greaves writes in the Moot's minute that the north now buys its fire from the south, and does not say whether this is good.
- **5 an Cèitean 2014 DE** — *The fourth currency reform*. Rìoghachd coinage is re-pegged to dubhan output rather than obsidian reserves for the first time — an economic admission, quietly made, of which resource actually runs the kingdom now.
- **3 an t-Ògmhios 2014 DE** — *The plain seal* (Cathair dhearg). The mint at Cathair dhearg stops pressing obsidian ink into the coinage seal. The new seal is plain. Fearchar Bonn's first dies are given to the library, where they are kept in the case beside the Guild of Hewers' oath-stone.
- **31 an t-Iuchar 2014 DE** — *The Rite's protest on the seal* (Seann Skell). The high custodian at Seann Skell protests the plain seal to the council as a sign that the kingdom no longer holds the vein sacred. The council's answer is that the kingdom never said it did. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh copies both letters into the chronicle.
- **27 am Màrt 2015 DE** — *The western pit towns meet* (Muileann àrsaidh). Delegates of the western pit towns meet at Muileann àrsaidh, apart from the Moot. They agree to go on working their seams and to sell their coal to any household in the north that will buy it.
- **6 an Giblean 2015 DE** — *Àth naomh joins the pit towns* (Àth naomh). Àth naomh, a Tuathaich town of the western hills with only a few old shafts, joins the pit towns' agreement, its delegates saying that the town would rather be cold with its neighbours than warm alone.
- **25 an Giblean 2015 DE** — *Tuathaich resistance organizes*. A cluster of northern communities refuse to fold into the new economy, continuing to work the last workable coal seams rather than trade independence for dependence on one man's fuel.
- **24 an Cèitean 2015 DE** — *The holdout towns* (Àth leathan). The towns that refuse are Àth leathan, Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais, Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg in the western hills. Their spokeswoman is Ruth Calder, a pit captain's daughter from Àth leathan. The Moot at Caol mhòr does not join them and does not condemn them.
- **4 an t-Samhain 2015 DE** — *Tom Varley's pits* (Cnoc thais). At Cnoc thais the pit captain Tom Varley reopens two shafts that had lain abandoned since the humans' time. The coal from them is poor. It is theirs, and it heats the town.
- **30 am Faoilleach 2016 DE** — *Tobar dhearg of the hills* (Tobar dhearg). Tobar dhearg in the western hills, the smallest of the holdout towns, has one pit and forty hewers. It sends its coal to Cathair gheal on the coast and receives fish in exchange.
- **7 an Gearran 2016 DE** — *Ellen Marsh's books* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh, a schoolteacher of Doire ghlas, finishes a collection of Tuathaich accounts of the Severance and the settlement, taken down from the old in the north over many years. It fills eleven books. It is her request that goes to the library.
- **15 an Gearran 2016 DE** — *The library's Tuathaich wing proposed* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). A formal request to archive Tuathaich oral history alongside the official Ròdaich record is submitted to Leabharlann Muileann chaol. It is tabled, not rejected — and remains tabled to this day.
- **12 an Lùnastal 2016 DE** — *The keeper's answer* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Raghnall mac Mhuirich's answer to Ellen Marsh says that the request awaits the council's view on the standing of oral testimony. The council has not given one.
- **20 an Lùnastal 2016 DE** — *Ellen Marsh's reply* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh writes back to the keeper that oral testimony was good enough for the census clerks when they took the Moot's figures. Her letter is filed with the request.
- **21 an Gearran 2017 DE** — *The coal price in the north* (Doire ghlas). The holdout pits sell their coal to Tuathaich households across the north at less than the price of dubhan. The Moot's own wool mills at Doire ghlas buy it. The Board's revenue from the north falls for the first time since the Severance.
- **22 am Màrt 2017 DE** — *The Board's northern revenue* (Cathair mhòr). The Mine Board's accounts show its northern revenue down by a quarter. The Board's report to the council names the western pits as the cause and the Leòid ruling as the remedy.
- **20 an Giblean 2017 DE** — *The seams declared Crown property* (Seann Bhral). The Mine Board declares the western seams Crown property under the Leòid ruling, holding that the right to work them lapsed when the holders stopped paying the fifth. The holders say they stopped paying when the Board stopped carrying the coal. The pits are ordered closed.
- **16 an Dàmhair 2017 DE** — *Enforcers posted to the west* (Seann Skell). A company of the Board's enforcers is posted at Seann Skell on the western coast to close the pits. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh notes that it is the first armed company the kingdom has sent toward the north since the Severance.
- **23 am Faoilleach 2018 DE** — *The enforcers' depot* (Seann Skell). The enforcers at Seann Skell on the west coast build a dubhan depot for their lorries at the town's edge. The town's Scorpion house refuses to bless it, and the high custodian of the Rite sends a priest to do so instead.
- **31 an Lùnastal 2018 DE** — *The Moot's warning* (Caol mhòr). Martha Greaves writes to the council from Caol mhòr that the western towns will not close their pits for a letter, and asks for a year's delay while the Moot talks with them. The letter is received and filed.
- **29 an t-Sultain 2018 DE** — *First skirmishes*. Minor, unrecorded clashes between state enforcers and Tuathaich coal-holdouts begin — too small individually to name, together the clear runway into open war.
- **28 an Dàmhair 2018 DE** — *The chronicler asks* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). At the foot of the year Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes that clashes are reported in the west, that the Board's reports of them are not given to the chronicler, and that she has asked for them. They were not given.
- **26 an t-Samhain 2018 DE** — *The pit-heads walled* (Muileann àrsaidh). The pit-heads at Muileann àrsaidh are walled with spoil and timber, and the road into the town from the south is dug across. The Board's enforcers at Seann Skell report the town closed to them.
- **25 an Dùbhlachd 2018 DE** — *Ruth Calder's letter* (Àth leathan). Ruth Calder writes to the council for the western towns, offering to pay the Crown's fifth in coal if the Board will carry it and let the pits work until the seams are spent. The letter reached the library. No answer to it did.
- **23 am Faoilleach 2019 DE** — *The Moot stands apart* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr resolves that it is not a party to the quarrel between the Board and the western towns, and will feed anyone who comes to its towns hungry. The resolution is carried by nine votes.
- **4 an t-Iuchar 2019 DE** — *The Moot's granaries* (Doire ghlas). The Moot orders its granaries at Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas filled beyond the usual, paying from the wool-mill revenue. The minute gives no reason.
- **2 an Lùnastal 2019 DE** — *Sìleas nic Rath* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh lays down the office, and Sìleas nic Rath, her clerk, becomes royal chronicler. Her record of the war is the one the library would later seal.
- **28 an Dàmhair 2019 DE** — *The mobilization order*. Regiments not called to active service since the Severance itself are reformed and re-equipped, openly, months before anyone in power admits a war is coming.
- **26 an t-Samhain 2019 DE** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn* (Cathair dhearg). Command of the reformed regiments is given to Somhairle mac Lachlainn, who had risen among the Board's enforcers. The rolls of the Severance companies are brought out of the council's chests at Cathair dhearg to name the reformed regiments, and the old names are read aloud before new men.
- **25 an Dùbhlachd 2019 DE** — *The Moot's last petition* (Cathair dhearg). Martha Greaves carries a petition from the Moot to the council at Cathair dhearg in person, asking that the western pits be left to work out their seams, which the Moot says will be spent within a few years in any case. It is received and filed. She is the first speaker of the Moot to enter the council chamber.
- **12 am Faoilleach 2020 DE** — *Arms by the ore line* (Seann Bhral). The Rail Board carries arms and dubhan from Cathair dhearg to Seann Bhral on the ore line and its western branch. The yard at Muileann chrom works day and night on the trains.
- **20 am Faoilleach 2020 DE** — *The hewers gather at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). Hewers from the five western towns gather at Àth leathan, where the road from the south enters the hills. The Board's lists name Ruth Calder and Tom Varley among them.
- **28 am Faoilleach 2020 DE** — *The regiments go west* (Seann Skell). The reformed regiments set out from Cathair dhearg by the western road, their carts and lorries running on dubhan, to join the enforcers at Seann Skell on the west coast.
- **11 an Giblean 2020 DE** — *Battle of Àth leathan* (Àraich Àth leathan). The first major engagement of An Cogadh Fada, the Long War. The state, already leaning on Dubhan's fuel to prop up its fading power, moves against the holdouts directly.
- **11 an Giblean 2020 DE** — *The dead of Àth leathan* (Àraich Àth leathan). The open record counts the kingdom's dead at Àth leathan and does not count the holdouts'. Tuathaich telling puts theirs in the hundreds. Ruth Calder's name does not appear in the open record after this battle.
- **11 an Giblean 2020 DE** — *Into the hills* (Muileann àrsaidh). After Àth leathan the holdouts give up the southern pits and fall back into the hills around Muileann àrsaidh and Cnoc thais. The pits at Àth leathan are taken without a fight and flooded on the Board's order.
- **13 an Giblean 2020 DE** — *An seachdamh rèisimeid raised* (Seann Skell). The seventh regiment is raised from the levies of the west coast and stationed at Seann Skell, the port nearest the western hills. It holds the road behind the army and the field of Àth leathan.
- **21 an Giblean 2020 DE** — *The field of Àth leathan after* (Àraich Àth leathan). The field of Àth leathan is left unploughed. The seventh regiment's patrols pass it on the road to the western hills and report it empty.
- **29 an Giblean 2020 DE** — *The wartime tithe*. A temporary tax increase, justified by the war, on every dubhan transaction in the kingdom. It is never repealed once the war ends.
- **7 an Cèitean 2020 DE** — *The tithe at the pumps* (Fèill Muileann òg). The wartime tithe is collected at the dubhan depots, where a clerk of the Treasury sits beside every pump. The fair-court at Muileann òg records the first complaint against it within a month.
- **13 an Cèitean 2020 DE** — *A' chiad rèisimeid raised* (Inis mhòr). The first regiment is raised at Inis mhòr, the port beside the capital, from the capital's own companies. It guards the council, the mint and the bridge over the Abhainn dhomhain.
- **20 an Cèitean 2020 DE** — *A' chiad chabhlach raised* (Àth gharbh). The first fleet is raised from the south-west harbours and stationed at Àth gharbh. It is sent round the western cape to stop coal going out by sea from the Tuathaich ports.
- **21 an Cèitean 2020 DE** — *An ceathramh cabhlach raised* (Cuan shean). The fourth fleet is raised at Cuan shean on the west coast and joins the first off the Tuathaich shore. Between them they close Seann Skell and Cnoc bhàn in the north-west to every boat but fishing boats, and search those.
- **5 an t-Ògmhios 2020 DE** — *The siege of Muileann àrsaidh* (Muileann àrsaidh). The regiments invest Muileann àrsaidh. The town holds for weeks on stored coal and potatoes, and its pit-heads are taken one at a time. Sìleas nic Rath's open record gives the day it fell and nothing else.
- **13 an t-Ògmhios 2020 DE** — *An treas rèisimeid raised* (Cathair mhòr). The third regiment is raised at Cathair mhòr, where the Mine Board keeps its offices in the old stone house of Mac Ùisdein. Its first muster is held under the market cross the house had raised.
- **21 an t-Ògmhios 2020 DE** — *An còigeamh rèisimeid raised* (Seann Warr). The fifth regiment is raised at Seann Warr on the west coast below the capital. It is sent north to relieve the regiments before Muileann àrsaidh.
- **29 an t-Ògmhios 2020 DE** — *The capital's lamp-houses rationed* (Cathair dhearg). Dubhan for the army is taken ahead of every other use. The capital's poorer streets go dark again, as they had before the fuel came, and the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg ration by street.
- **17 an t-Iuchar 2020 DE** — *Families at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Families from the western pits come into Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas with what they can carry. The Moot feeds them from its own stores, as it had resolved. The council sends nothing and forbids nothing.
- **25 an t-Iuchar 2020 DE** — *The Moot's granaries opened* (Caol mhòr). The Moot opens its granaries at Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas to the families from the west. Its minute records the amount given and the names of the families, which are among the few Tuathaich records of the war the library does not hold.
- **2 an Lùnastal 2020 DE** — *Agnes Pike's school as a shelter* (Doire ghlas). The school at Doire ghlas that Agnes Pike founded is given over to the families from the west, its benches used for beds. Ellen Marsh, who teaches there, takes down the families' accounts.
- **10 an Lùnastal 2020 DE** — *Cnoc thais taken* (Cnoc thais). Cnoc thais is taken after the regiments cut the road to its pits. Tom Varley's two shafts are fired and sealed. The open record gives the number of holdouts taken and not the number who went on into the hills.
- **23 an t-Sultain 2020 DE** — *An dàrna cabhlach raised* (Seann Skell). The second fleet is raised at Seann Skell on the southern coast to keep the eastern and southern waters while the first and fourth are in the north-west.
- **2 an Dàmhair 2020 DE** — *Raiders take the salt-boats* (Spùinneadairean-mara). With the fleets drawn north-west, raiders from the eastern waters take two salt-boats off Àth bheag and burn a third. The second fleet runs one of the raiders down off Baile ìseal.
- **17 an Dàmhair 2020 DE** — *An siathamh rèisimeid raised* (Cnoc bheag). The sixth regiment is raised at Cnoc bheag, the great port of the Hawk houses on the north-central coast. It holds the northern road between the Tuathaich shires and the middle of the island, and the Hawk houses bless its colours in their own order.
- **25 an Dàmhair 2020 DE** — *An dàrna rèisimeid raised* (Àth dhìreach). The second regiment is raised at Àth dhìreach in the east and set to guard the ore line and the library road. Its camp is the first soldiery the town of Muileann chaol has seen.
- **2 an t-Samhain 2020 DE** — *An ceathramh rèisimeid raised* (Caol bheag). The fourth regiment is raised at Caol bheag on the north-east coast. It is shipped west round the north coast in hired dubhan hulls and landed at Ceann mhòr in the Tuathaich north.
- **10 an t-Samhain 2020 DE** — *The regiments at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). The fourth regiment is quartered at Ceann mhòr, in the old human magistrate's house that the maor had kept since the shires were drawn. The Moot protests the quartering. The protest is received.
- **15 an t-Samhain 2020 DE** — *The fishermen of Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). The fleets off the north-west search the fishing boats of Cathair gheal every day they go out. The fishermen petition the Moot, which petitions the council. The searching goes on.
- **16 an t-Samhain 2020 DE** — *An t-ochdamh rèisimeid raised* (Inis uaine). The eighth regiment is raised at Inis uaine on the east coast to guard the dubhan depots and tanks of the eastern ports, which the council fears the holdouts might fire.
- **1 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE** — *An treas cabhlach raised* (Baile ghorm). The third fleet is raised at Baile ghorm on the south-west coast and carries the army's dubhan up the west coast in tank-hulls to the regiments in the hills.
- **9 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE** — *The Baile chrom vigil* (Baile chrom). The Grey Night cult at Baile chrom keeps its vigil as always. The regiments quartered along the coast report a night when the whole town was dark and silent, and search it, and find nothing.
- **17 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE** — *Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg* (Àth naomh). The last two western towns, Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg, open their roads to the regiments without a siege. Their pits are flooded. The open record names no holdouts taken at either.
- **25 an Dùbhlachd 2020 DE** — *An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised* (Seann Skell). The ninth regiment is raised at Seann Skell on the southern coast, the second of that name in the regimental list, to guard the dubhan works the shipmasters built there. The regimental clerks tell the two apart by their coasts.
- **29 an Dàmhair 2021 DE** — *The column goes south* (Muileann mhin). A column of holdouts, several hundred strong, leaves the western hills and moves south-east through the middle of the island toward the capital. Why it did so is in the sealed archive. The name Tuathaich telling gives its leader is Owen Barrow. The open record gives no name.
- **24 an t-Samhain 2021 DE** — *The column's road* (Àth bheag). The column's road south-east runs by Àth bheag in the west, Muileann mhin and the edge of the capital's country. The towns it passes report it, and the open record copies their reports and not the regiments'.
- **6 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *The camp by Muileann ghlas* (Muileann ghlas). The column passes Muileann òg and makes camp on the fields by Muileann ghlas, within a day's walk of Cathair dhearg. The first and third regiments are brought down the fair road to meet it.
- **9 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *The fair-ground emptied* (Fèill Muileann òg). The fair-ground at Muileann òg is cleared of its standing booths to give the first and third regiments room to camp. Its court's books for the year end without a closing entry.
- **10 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *Battle of Muileann ghlas* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). The war's second and final major battle. The Tuathaich holdouts are broken within a single year's campaign — descendants of the humans once pushed to the island's edge, pushed back again, this time by a fuel one of their own invented.
- **10 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *The field at Muileann ghlas* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). The open record lists the first and third regiments on the field at Muileann ghlas and gives no count of the column's dead. The regiments' own dead are named on a stone at Cathair mhòr, set up the following year.
- **10 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *The last pits give up* (Àraich Àth leathan). Word of Muileann ghlas reaches the hills, and the holdouts still in them come down to the seventh regiment's posts on the Àth leathan road. They are disarmed and sent home. The open record counts their weapons.
- **10 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *An Cogadh Fada ends*. Nine regiments and four fleets, still active today, were raised in this campaign; each is named for the town it is stationed in.
- **10 an Dùbhlachd 2021 DE** — *Fadachadh* (Caol mhòr). Among Tuathaich speakers, 'chaidh am fadachadh', they got long-warred, begins to be said of the defeat in the west, and then of any defeat after holding out too long. It is said as a joke, and the people who say it do not laugh.
- **13 am Faoilleach 2022 DE** — *The regiments stay on their stations* (Cathair dhearg). The nine regiments and four fleets are not stood down. The council keeps each at the town it was raised in and pays them from the wartime tithe.
- **26 am Faoilleach 2022 DE** — *The dubhan monopoly completes*. With the last organized resistance gone, Dubhan's fuel becomes functionally mandatory across the entire island economy.
- **11 an Gearran 2022 DE** — *The western seams flooded* (Àth leathan). By the Board's order the last western seams are flooded and their shafts capped with concrete. The seventh regiment stands by at each capping. No coal is dug on the island outside the Board's own works after this.
- **24 an Gearran 2022 DE** — *The prisoners sent home* (Caol mhòr). The holdouts held since Muileann ghlas are released from the capital's gaol and sent north under the first regiment's escort as far as the boundary stones. The Moot's register adds their names to the dead and maimed it has kept since the Severance, in a column of its own.
- **4 an t-Iuchar 2022 DE** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn seated* (Cathair dhearg). Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given a seat on the council. He is the first soldier to sit there since the captains of the Severance war.
- **31 an Lùnastal 2022 DE** — *The seventh regiment at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). The seventh regiment builds a post on the road below Àth leathan and keeps a company there. The post is called the Àth leathan post in the regimental lists and something else in the town.
- **15 an Dùbhlachd 2022 DE** — *The stone at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). A stone is set up at Cathair mhòr with the names of the regiments' dead from Àth leathan and Muileann ghlas. It stands beside the market cross of the house of Mac Ùisdein.
- **28 an Dùbhlachd 2022 DE** — *The Muileann ghlas field* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). The field at Muileann ghlas where the column camped is sown again. The farmer who holds it finds weapons in the furrows for years and hands them to the first regiment, which keeps a list.
- **27 an Giblean 2023 DE** — *The library's war archive sealed* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Leabharlann Muileann chaol's complete Long War record is formally sealed from public access for a term of fifty years — the only sealed archive in the kingdom's history.
- **22 an Cèitean 2023 DE** — *Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). What remains open of the royal chronicle for the war years is Sìleas nic Rath's list of places, the regiments present and the counts she was allowed. Her full record went into the sealed archive with the rest.
- **26 an Cèitean 2023 DE** — *The cairn at Àth leathan* (Àraich Àth leathan). Tuathaich families build a cairn on the field of Àth leathan without leave. The seventh regiment's patrols leave it standing, and it grows by a stone or two every time the patrols pass.
- **2 an Lùnastal 2023 DE** — *The tithe carried forward* (Cathair dhearg). The Treasury's accounts carry the wartime tithe forward as a standing line under the regiments' pay. No minute of the council records a decision to keep it.
- **29 an t-Sultain 2023 DE** — *The Fuel-Fitters and the regiments* (Seann Skell). The Guild of Fuel-Fitters at Seann Skell on the southern coast is given the contract for the regiments' engines and the fleets' hulls, and doubles its rolls. The rule of the charter holds, and all its new fitters are Ròdaich.
- **28 an Dàmhair 2023 DE** — *The second fleet off Baile ìseal* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The second fleet runs down the raiders off Baile ìseal who had taken the salt-boats during the war, and brings their hulls into Seann Skell. The lighthouse log at Baile ìseal records the chase from the lamp-room.
- **23 an Giblean 2024 DE** — *The fourth fleet in the north-west* (Spùinneadairean-mara). The fourth fleet, kept on the Tuathaich coast after the war, searches the raiders' bays off Cathair gheal and finds them empty. The fishermen of Cathair gheal say the raiders left when the fleets came and will be back when they go.
- **25 an Cèitean 2024 DE** — *The third fleet's tank-hulls* (Baile ghorm). The third fleet at Baile ghorm keeps its tank-hulls after the war and runs dubhan up the west coast to the Tuathaich depots on the council's contract. The Moot pays the freight.
- **2 an t-Ògmhios 2024 DE** — *The creature off the cape again* (Uilebheist na Mara). The fourth fleet's log for the year records a thing longer than a patrol boat off the north-west cape, where the Tuathaich fishermen had reported one in Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's time. The log records it as a whale.
- **10 an t-Ògmhios 2024 DE** — *Anna nic Phàil's motion* (Cathair dhomhain). The proposal to compensate the Tuathaich communities is carried into the council by Anna nic Phàil, councillor for Cathair dhomhain, on a petition from the Moot under Martha Greaves. She speaks for it once.
- **18 an t-Ògmhios 2024 DE** — *The reparations debate* (Cathair dhearg). A proposal to formally compensate Tuathaich communities for wartime losses is raised in the capital and quietly allowed to die without a vote.
- **27 an Dàmhair 2024 DE** — *The Moot's minute on the reparations* (Caol mhòr). The Moot's minute on the reparations motion runs to one line: 'Allowed to die.' Martha Greaves lays down the chair the same year. The Moot chooses Peter Hale, a great-grandson of its first speaker, to follow her.
- **6 an Dùbhlachd 2024 DE** — *The fifth regiment's barracks* (Seann Warr). The fifth regiment builds stone barracks at Seann Warr, the first permanent quarters any of the nine regiments has had. The town gives the land and takes the regiment's custom.
- **14 an Dùbhlachd 2024 DE** — *The eighth regiment at Inis uaine* (Inis uaine). The eighth regiment's guard on the eastern dubhan tanks at Inis uaine is made permanent. The regiment's officers take houses in the town, and Inis uaine's Seann Spioradan house adds the regiment to its prayers.
- **22 an Dùbhlachd 2024 DE** — *The fourth regiment leaves Ceann mhòr* (Caol bheag). The fourth regiment leaves the old magistrate's house at Ceann mhòr and goes home to Caol bheag. The Moot asks for the house to be given to the town. It is given to the maor.
- **18 an Giblean 2025 DE** — *Seann-chunntas* (Caol mhòr). Tuathaich speakers begin to name the tabled archive request and the dead reparations motion together as 'seann-chunntas', an old reckoning that nobody in power will act on and nobody has cancelled. Official Ròdaich usage does not take the word up.
- **17 an Cèitean 2025 DE** — *The Sloc Mòr closed* (Achadh dhomhain). The Mine Board closes the upper galleries of the Sloc Mòr at Achadh dhomhain. One face is kept open under the custody of the Rite, to cut ore for the altars, a few baskets a year.
- **29 an Cèitean 2025 DE** — *The last hewers* (Achadh dhomhain). Twelve hewers are kept at the Sloc Mòr to cut the altar-ore under the Rite's custody. They are the last of their trade working the vein on the island, and the Rite gives them its own oath, not the dissolved guild's.
- **15 an t-Ògmhios 2025 DE** — *The regiments at the Còmhrag* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). Fighters from the regiments are entered in the Còmhrag at Ceann leathan for the first time. The ninth regiment's man wins it. The fair-wardens raise the gate-price again.
- **27 an t-Ògmhios 2025 DE** — *The second regiment's library guard* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The second regiment at Àth dhìreach keeps a guard at Leabharlann Muileann chaol on the sealed war archive. The keeper, Raghnall mac Mhuirich, writes to the council that the library had not asked for one.
- **14 an t-Iuchar 2025 DE** — *The ore line carries no ore* (Achadh dhomhain). The last ore train runs from Achadh dhomhain to Cathair dhearg. The ore line keeps its name and carries dubhan, wool and soldiers.
- **12 an Lùnastal 2025 DE** — *The sixth regiment on the northern road* (Caol mhòr). The sixth regiment at Cnoc bheag keeps posts on the northern road where the boundary stones stand. Tuathaich going south show a pass for the first time since the Severance. The council's minute calls the passes temporary.
- **10 an t-Sultain 2025 DE** — *The fair of the present year* (Fèill Muileann òg). The fair at Muileann òg draws traders from every shire the state controls. Tuathaich wool is sold there on its northern day, through Ròdaich factors, as it has been since the first fair.
- **9 an Dàmhair 2025 DE** — *The Còmhrag of the present year* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). The Còmhrag at Ceann leathan is fought with staves and fists, as it has been since edged tools were banned. Two regiments and nine shires send fighters. One man dies.
- **7 an t-Samhain 2025 DE** — *The eleven books* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh's eleven books are copied by hand in the Tuathaich schools and kept in the north. The library's catalogue lists the tabled request and not the books.
- **19 am Faoilleach 2026 DE** — *The Moot of the present year* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr meets under Peter Hale. Its minute-books run unbroken from Walter Hale's first meeting. It has no standing in Ròdaich law and has never asked for any.
- **17 an Gearran 2026 DE** — *The dubhan works of the present* (Seann Skell). Dubhan is made at Seann Skell on the southern coast and at works in the east and north. Every lamp, engine, ship and lorry on the island runs on it. The coinage is pegged to it, and the tithe is taken on every sale.
- **29 an t-Iuchar 2026 DE** — *The altar-ore* (Seann Skell). The Rite's twelve hewers at the Sloc Mòr cut the year's altar-ore. It fills four baskets. The high custodian at Seann Skell divides it among the houses of the Rite by lot.
- **22 an t-Samhain 2026 DE** — *The chronicler's note on the present* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Sìleas nic Rath writes at the foot of the year that the kingdom's record is complete in every part but two: the war, which is sealed, and the north, which was not asked.
- **21 an Dùbhlachd 2026 DE** — *The present* (Cathair dhearg). The coal is all but gone. The dubhan economy runs on a name that used to belong to one man. The Ròdaich hold the capital and the sea. The Tuathaich hold the north, a grievance five years old, and a First-Canoe memory the people who twice defeated them still call folklore.

## Appendix A — The Rulers and Houses of Rodos

This appendix sets out the lines of those who ruled on Rodos, age by age, as the surviving lists give them: the two oral lists of the Ancient Age; the Keepers' roll and the king-list of the Holy Age; the crown of the Age of Sundering as the custody-book and the king-list record it; the council, the Commissioners and the overseers of the Age of Strangers; and the rulers of the restored kingdom. After the tables come short accounts of each line, an account of the seven houses of custody, and an account of how the keeping of the vein and the keeping of the realm were joined and parted.

The tables give only rulers whom the lists and chronicles name. Where a list says that names are missing, the table says so, and gives none. A reign is dated by the rolls that record its beginning and its end. Where no roll marks one or the other, the table gives "—". Where the rolls fix it only roughly, the year is marked *c.* Many rulers are known only from a single mention in the middle of their reign. For these the table gives "in office" and the year of that mention.

### I. The Tables

**The Stone Kings of Dùn ìseal (Rìghrean na Cloiche), Age I.** The oldest oral list, held on the hill of Dùn ìseal. It "gives no lengths of reign" (9 an Lùnastal 7600 BDE). The year shown is the year of the deed each king's telling remembers. It is not a year of accession.

| No. | Name | Byname | Came to rule | Told of in | The reign |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ailean Mòr | the great | first in the list | 7600 BDE | Held the hill where Dùn ìseal now stands and threw up its first ring of bank |
| 2 | Gormshuil nic Ailein | — | second in the list | 7574 BDE | The first woman in any list; brought the herds to the warm springs in a hard winter and lost none |
| 3 | Dòmhnall Clachach | of the stones | third in the list | 7494 BDE | Set the boundary stones of the valley grazing, some still standing and still argued over |
| 4 | Fearchar Bacach | the lame | after the first named storm | 7374 BDE | Carried to the gatherings in a chair of woven birch; the first ruler remembered for a hurt |
| 5 | Mòrag Chruaidh | the hard | fifth in the list | 6929 BDE | Raided the salt-pans at Baile ghorm: the first war in either list, seven dead on the hill side |
| 6 | Iain Dubh | the black | sixth in the list | — to 6874 BDE | Went down to repeat the salt raid and was killed on the shingle at Baile ghorm |
| 7 | Raghnall Ceannfhionn | fair-headed | seventh in the list | 6426 BDE | Made the peace of the ford with the Red Hill: salt for wool |
