**Muileann chiar** (Achadh shean). Founded 10 an Gearran 2901 BDE by keepers of the sacred forest. Muileann chiar of Achadh shean stands at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the forest marked sacred before any faith claimed it. Its people were party to the holy-wood dispute of the Holy Age and have kept the forest's edge since. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It is not the silver town of the same name. Known for keepers of the sacred forest's edge.

**Muileann chiar** (Seann Bhral). Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 200 DE by millers of the Seann Bhral country. A dusky mill town with a citadel in the south-east, not the silver town of the same name further north; the confusion of the two is an old grievance here. It grinds for Àth chiar and the harbour of Seann Bhral. It keeps the old spirits. Known for the other Muileann chiar.

**Muileann chiar** (Muileann chiar). Founded 23 an t-Iuchar 326 DE by ore-crushers of the eastern diggings. Muileann chiar, seat of the province of the same name, began as an ore-crushing mill for the diggings in the hills east of the capital. It grew large in the Age of Strangers, when the district was worked by the ton, and lost its trade when Scàineadh Cill ghlas, a short way west, closed the district for a generation. It is not the silver town of the same name further east, and the two are often confused in the older records. Known for ore mills of the eastern district.

**Muileann chiar** (Dùn ìseal). Founded 10 an Lùnastal 2992 BDE by Ròdaich custodians who found the silver seam. Muileann chiar was founded when a silver seam was found near, but distinct from, the great vein, the island's first confirmed resource that was not obsidian. In the Age of Strangers human interests tried to claim the silver as well, and the Ròdaich kept it; the town grew alongside the obsidian workings as demand for both rose. It is smaller now than in its great years. Known for the island's silver seam.

**Muileann chrom** (Seann Skell). Founded 22 an Cèitean 1187 DE by Ròdaich millers of the Seann Skell country. A crooked mill on the edge of the north-west, left in Ròdaich hands when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed around it. It keeps the faith of the Yellow Scorpion like its Tuathaich neighbours, and its millers have ground for both peoples since the Severance, which the chroniclers note without comment. Cnoc ghlas and Àth àrsaidh over the line buy its flour. Known for a Ròdaich mill on the Tuathaich line.

**Muileann chrom** (Muileann chrom). Founded 11 an Gearran 2994 BDE by Ròdaich millers on the river bend. The mill on the bend of the river gave its name to the town and then to the province, of which it is the seat and the largest place. It ground grain for the whole central country and, in the Age of Strangers, for the camps east of it as well. It is a busy, unwalled town that has never needed walls, standing between Cathair mhòr and Ceann leathan on the road that joins them. Known for the great mill on the river bend.

**Muileann chrom** (Tobar fhiadhaich). Founded 27 an Gearran 432 DE by millers of Tobar fhiadhaich. A mill town on the north coast, grinding for Tobar fhiadhaich and the upland farms behind it. It is one of several places named Muileann chrom and is not the great mill town of the central country. It is a quiet town of millers and inshore fishers. Known for north-coast mill of Tobar fhiadhaich.

**Muileann dhearg** (Inis bheag). Founded 15 an Giblean 1527 DE by red-stone millers. A red mill town beside Muileann fhada in the north-east, the two together grinding for Doire chiar. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for red mill beside Muileann fhada.

**Muileann dhearg** (Muileann dhearg). Founded 2 an t-Ògmhios 1798 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the central country. The red mill is the seat of its province and one of the largest towns of the centre, standing between Seann Chwen and Cnoc ghorm. Its mills stamped ore in the Age of Strangers and turned back to grain after the Severance. It is a town of the capital's faith, busy and unwalled. Known for stamping mills turned to grain.

**Muileann dhearg** (Muileann chrom). Founded 26 an Gearran 758 DE by millers of Muileann chrom. A walled mill town on the road north of Muileann chrom, one of three places named Muileann dhearg. It was walled in the Age of Strangers to protect its stores. It follows the capital's faith. Known for walled red mill.

**Muileann dhearg** (Muileann dhearg). Founded 30 an t-Sultain 38 BDE by ore-millers of the central diggings. Muileann dhearg, seat of its province, is a mill town a short way from Cill ghlas. Scàineadh Cill ghlas tore open the hills nearby and killed dozens, and the town's mills stood idle for a generation after. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for red mill beside Cill ghlas.

**Muileann dhomhain** (Muileann dhomhain). Founded 8 an t-Iuchar 1252 BDE by the millers of the deep race. A mill on a deep, fast race in the central country and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain. It was a milling town for centuries and grew rich carrying grain to the mining settlements in the Age of Strangers, when the camps could no longer feed themselves. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and its grain-exchange still sets the price of flour for the south-east. Known for the grain-exchange of the south-east.

**Muileann dhomhain** (Dùn ìseal). Founded 23 am Màrt 362 BDE by Ròdaich millers of Dùn ìseal. The deep mill takes its name from a mill-race cut far down into the rock to reach a steady flow. It grinds for Dùn dhearg and the villages around it and has done so since the Holy Age. The folk tradition of the ancestors holds here, and each new millstone is blessed at the hearth before it is set. Known for its deep-cut mill-race.

**Muileann dhomhain** (Muileann dhomhain). Founded 9 an t-Samhain 1582 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the south-east. Muileann dhomhain, seat of its province, is a town of twenty thousand built around deep mill-pools fed from the hills. Its flour goes down to the quays of Ceann chaol and out by sea, and the two towns have depended on each other since the Holy Age. It is not the smaller Muileann dhomhain of Dùn ìseal to the north. Known for deep mill-pools feeding Ceann chaol's ships.

**Muileann dhubh** (Achadh naomh). Founded 27 an Dùbhlachd 980 DE by millers of Achadh naomh. The black mill stands on the northern road near Tobar ghorm, grinding for the villages of Achadh naomh province. Its wheel was darkened, the old telling says, by ore dust carried downstream from the mining roads. It is a small town and has always been one. Known for black mill of the northern road.

**Muileann dhìreach** (Achadh chaol). Founded 17 an Lùnastal 1567 BDE by the custodian house of Achadh chaol. Muileann dhìreach was raised to grind the barley of Achadh chaol, and its mill-race still runs straight as a ruled line from the stream above the town. In the Age of Strangers it ground for the camps as well as for its own people, and the tithe clerks kept a counting-room beside the wheel. A reading-house of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh stands on the square, and the miller's guild and the school have shared its bell since before anyone wrote the arrangement down. Known for grain mills on the straight race.

**Muileann fhada** (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Founded 8 an Dàmhair 2449 BDE by millers of the northern mining road. Muileann fhada, the long mill, is a small walled town on the old mining road of the north. An Taigh-seinnse Reòta stands at its edge, one of the great taverns of the old circuit. Colbh Cnoc chiar stands to the west, and the town's people say the stone's two words are older than any mill. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the mining road.

**Muileann fhada** (Baile ghorm). Founded 16 an t-Samhain 578 DE by millers of the house of Tormod mac Ruairidh. A long mill-race cut beside a south-eastern stream gave the town its name and its living, grinding the grain of the farms about the other Baile ghorm. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the roads past Làrach an Dùin carried ore-wagons and the thieves who followed them. It keeps the old spirits, and the millers still leave the first sack of each season at the race-head for the ancestors. Cnoc bhàn on the hill above buys most of its flour. Known for the long mill-race and first-sack offering.

**Muileann fhada** (Doire chiar). Founded 10 am Màrt 746 DE by millers of Doire chiar. A long mill in the north-east beside Muileann dhearg, grinding for the large village of Doire chiar. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for flour for Doire chiar.

**Muileann fhada** (Cnoc bhàn). Founded 21 an Giblean 1759 BDE by millers of the Ros fhionn river. A long mill-house on the Ros fhionn gave the place its name, and a river quay below it made it a port, sending flour downstream by barge. Its walls date from the Age of Strangers, when a tithe store was kept here and needed guarding. Trade on the river dried up when the carts took the traffic, and the crossing of Drochaid Ros fhionn just upstream is now rarely used; the town has shrunk to its walls. Known for a river port gone quiet.

**Muileann fhionn** (Caol mhòr). Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 1802 DE by human administrators of the northern landing. Muileann fhionn was built as a fort and mill by human administrators in the Age of Strangers, to guard the northern landing. After the Severance it became a Tuathaich town. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith. Known for strangers' fort of the north.

**Muileann fhionn** (Seann Chwen). Founded 1 an Cèitean 1365 DE by millers of the Ceann leathan country. A fair-stoned walled mill town between Ceann leathan and Cuan dhearg, grinding grain landed at both harbours. Its walls went up in the Age of Strangers. It follows the Dark Unicorn. Known for grain milled for two harbours.

**Muileann gharbh** (Cnoc dhubh). Founded 12 am Màrt 1812 DE by a human ore concern. Muileann gharbh, the rough mill, was built in the Age of Strangers to crush ore on the road down to the eastern harbours. When the mountain was worked day and night the mill never stopped, and the town grew no larger than the mill needed. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh, which found many hearers among the mill hands. Known for rough mill of the ore road.

**Muileann gheal** (Dùn dhearg). Founded 7 an Dàmhair 1043 DE by white-stone millers. A white stone mill in the south-east that grinds for the city of Dùn dhearg. It keeps the old spirits and is a large mill-town with a guild of millers older than the city's walls. Known for flour for Dùn dhearg.

**Muileann gheal** (Muileann chiar). Founded 20 an Lùnastal 1841 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Muileann gheal was a walled mill-camp under the Doire uaine hills, built in the Age of Strangers to crush ore from the eastern diggings. It is small, fewer than seven hundred people. The warm springs of Muileann ruadh lie a short walk away, and the camp's miners bathed there. Known for walled mill-camp under Doire uaine.

**Muileann ghlas** (Dùn chrom). Founded 16 an t-Samhain 2251 BDE by Ròdaich millers of Dùn chrom. The grey mill is an old grain town near the fair at Muileann òg and within a day of the capital. It is remembered above all for the Battle of Muileann ghlas, the second and final major battle of An Cogadh Fada, fought on its fields, in which the Tuathaich holdouts were broken. The battlefield, Àraich Muileann ghlas, lies just north-west of the town. Known for the last battle of the Long War.

**Muileann leathan** (Muileann àrsaidh). Founded 23 an Lùnastal 1942 DE by Tuathaich millers. Muileann leathan of the north-west was built by Tuathaich settlers soon after the Severance to grind grain for the northern villages, which had lost the Ròdaich mills to the south. It is a small town, and its mill-race was dug by hand by the first households. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith. Known for Tuathaich grain mill.

**Muileann leathan** (Cnoc dhubh). Founded 15 an Dùbhlachd 1253 BDE by the millers of the wide stream. A broad mill on a slow river, old enough that its founding is recorded only in the king-lists of the Holy Age. It grinds for the coast-town of Seann Mhorn and for the villages round Àth àrsaidh, and its people keep the old spirits. The temple ruins of Làrach an Teampaill lie in the hills behind it, and the millers will not quarry them. Known for wide mill-wheels, grain for Seann Mhorn.

**Muileann leathan** (Muileann leathan). Founded 24 an Giblean 303 BDE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. A wide mill on a northern river, walled with a citadel, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann leathan. It was a Ròdaich town until the Severance, when the Tuathaich took it over as one of the principal towns of their homeland. It is a centre of Creideamh nan Tuathach, and its keep is where the Tuathaich northern coast is governed. Known for the Tuathaich mill-citadel.

**Muileann leathan** (Ceann mhin). Founded 16 an Dàmhair 1384 DE by millers of Ceann mhin. A walled mill town a short way inland from Ceann mhin, whose broad mill-pool is the largest on that coast. It was walled when Ceann mhin was, in the Age of Strangers, to protect its stores. Its flour goes to the ships at Ceann mhin and never to the rival quays of Ceann chaol. Known for broad mill serving Ceann mhin.

**Muileann mhin** (Baile fhiadhaich). Founded 18 an Gearran 1560 DE by millers of the west. Muileann mhin of Baile fhiadhaich is a mill town of the west, founded in the long quiet centuries on a stream that turns smooth stones. It grinds for the harbour at Baile fhiadhaich. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith, and its millers are known for honest measures. Known for smooth-stone mill of the west.

**Muileann mhin** (Muileann mhin). Founded 20 an t-Iuchar 1541 BDE by millers of the capital shore. Muileann mhin is a large harbour town east of the capital and the seat of its province. Its flour mills have fed the capital since the Holy Age. It keeps the capital's faith and ships its flour along the shore to Cathair dhearg and Ros dhomhain. Known for the capital's flour mills.

**Muileann mhin** (Tobar ghorm). Founded 8 an t-Iuchar 617 DE by millers of Tobar ghorm. Muileann mhin grinds the fine flour of Tobar ghorm, a short way east, and has risen and fallen with the larger village's harvests in every age. Its wheels are the oldest still turning in the province, and the miller families keep a roll of their masters going back to the Age of Sundering. In fair season the carts from the wool fairs come back loaded with its flour. Known for fine flour for Tobar ghorm.

**Muileann naomh** (Muileann naomh). Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios 2400 BDE by priests of the Yellow Scorpion. A holy mill in the west, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose wheel is said to have been consecrated to Cnut. It lies near the Àth leathan battlefield and was taken over by crown regiments in the Long War. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the consecrated mill-wheel.

**Muileann naomh** (Muileann naomh). Founded 16 an t-Iuchar 88 DE by priests of the Obsidian Rite. A holy mill in the south, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose priests of the orthodox Rite bless the grain before it is ground. It is one of the few towns of Creideamh nan Ròdach and trades with Caol ruadh and Seann Skell. Known for grain blessed by the Rite's priests.

**Muileann ruadh** (Doire fhionn). Founded 29 an Giblean 1416 BDE by Ròdaich millers of the north. Muileann ruadh of Doire fhionn is a mill town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. Its citadel was raised after the Severance to watch the Tuathaich border. It keeps the Hawk's rite. Known for red mill and border citadel.

**Muileann ruadh** (Cnoc naomh). Founded 14 an Lùnastal 1346 DE by red-sandstone millers. A small mill-town built of red sandstone, grinding for Baile chrom and the village of Cill fhada. It was never walled, relying on Baile chrom's walls in hard times. Its people keep the faith of Uallach, and the mill-house has a small shrine to the Dark Unicorn above the wheel. Known for red sandstone mill-house.

**Muileann ruadh** (Dùn ìseal). Founded 11 an t-Ògmhios 2666 BDE by keepers of the hot springs. A red walled mill town beside Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, the hot springs whose warm water drives its wheel through winter. The springs were held sacred by the old spirits, and the town walled them against claims from the human administration. It is a place for the sick and the old to bathe. Known for the hot springs of Muileann ruadh.

**Muileann ruadh** (Cnoc leathan). Founded 15 am Faoilleach 151 DE by Ròdaich millers of Cnoc leathan. Muileann ruadh is a walled mill town near An Taigh-òsta Grianach, the great inn of the eastern road. Its walls were raised when the inns fortified before the war, and the town and the inn have shared a watch ever since. The unexplored hollow called Toll-dubh lies close by, and the townsfolk keep away from it. It is not the Muileann ruadh of the warm springs to the west. Known for red mill on the inn road.

**Muileann shean** (Muileann shean). Founded 1 an t-Samhain 2462 BDE by the first millers of the northern river. The old mill of the north, whose wheel the Holy Age king-lists already call ancient, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann shean. Its walls went up in the Age of Strangers, when it ground grain for the mining camps on contract and was raided for it. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and owns the well-village of Tobar ìseal below it. Known for the oldest mill-wheel in the north.

**Muileann uaine** (Muileann dhomhain). Founded 8 am Màrt 1827 DE by a human milling concern with Ròdaich labour. Muileann uaine was built in the Age of Strangers as a crushing mill for ore from the interior workings. It is not the Muileann uaine of the Cnoc bheag country that the Green Death struck, though the two are often confused. It is a small town now and keeps the orthodox Obsidian Rite. Known for ore-crushing mill of the interior workings.

**Muileann uaine** (Cnoc bheag). Founded 3 an t-Sultain 406 BDE by priests of the Hungry Hawk. A green mill in the wooded middle west, one of the few towns where Creideamh an t-Seabhaig, the Rite's older form, still holds. The carved hawk over the mill-door is said to be as old as the Binding of the First Flame. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and since then the second sense of 'uaine' has clung to its name. Known for the Hawk-faith mill.

**Muileann àrsaidh** (Muileann àrsaidh). Founded 10 an t-Iuchar 555 BDE by Ròdaich millers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Muileann àrsaidh, the ancient mill, is the seat of its province in the Tuathaich north-west, founded as a Ròdaich mill town in the Holy Age. It was walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The mill still grinds for the surrounding villages. Known for the old mill of the north-west.

**Muileann àrsaidh** (Muileann àrsaidh). Founded 2 an Gearran 621 BDE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. An ancient mill town of the north-west, and seat of Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A second Muileann àrsaidh lies close by, and the two are called the elder and the younger. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the elder of the two ancient mills.

**Muileann àrsaidh** (Cnoc thais). Founded 20 an Giblean 1740 DE by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. The younger of the two Muileann àrsaidhs, walled, a short distance from the elder. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the younger ancient mill.

**Muileann àrsaidh** (Dùn thais). Founded 19 am Faoilleach 1329 BDE by a custodian house of Dùn thais. Muileann àrsaidh is an ancient mill fortified with a citadel, a short way from Muileann chaol. The citadel guarded the road to the ore in the Holy Age and now guards the road to the library. It is a small place of fewer than two thousand. Known for fortified ancient mill.

**Muileann òg** (Dùn chrom). Founded 10 am Faoilleach 1950 DE by millers of the restored kingdom. Muileann òg, the young mill, was built in the first years of the restored kingdom. Its annual fair, Fèill Muileann òg, became the island's largest gathering. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies close by. Known for Fèill Muileann òg, the great fair.

**Ros bheag** (Ros bheag). Founded 4 am Faoilleach 1058 BDE by custodians of the western coast. Ros bheag is the citadel harbour and provincial seat of the western coast, holding Dùn thais and Ros àrsaidh within its province. It was fortified in the Holy Age and has been the western sea's naval station through every age since. Its people keep the Yellow Scorpion faith. Known for citadel harbour of the western coast.

**Ros bhàn** (Seann Chwen). Founded 24 an Lùnastal 65 DE by the garrison of the gulf mouth. Ros bhàn is a fortified headland at the mouth of the gulf, walled and given a citadel in the long quiet centuries to guard the harbours within. It is a city by rank, though most of its people are soldiers, customs clerks and their families. The white stone of its headland gives it its name. Known for fortified headland at the gulf mouth.

**Ros chiar** (Ceann bheag). Founded 1 an t-Iuchar 2992 BDE by the headland-lords of Ceann bheag. A dusky headland city on the north coast, walled, with a citadel on the rock and a harbour below. It was one of the harbours the human traders first used after the Crossing, and its citadel was taken and retaken in the war before the Severance. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and competes with Caol bheag for the northern trade. Known for the fortified headland harbour.

**Ros chiar** (Muileann bheag). Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1449 DE by fishers of Muileann bheag. A dusky headland harbour village on the north-east coast that ships the flour of Muileann bheag. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and competes with Seann Toll for the coast trade. Known for the flour harbour of Muileann bheag.

**Ros dhomhain** (Ros dhomhain). Founded 27 am Faoilleach 1232 DE by merchant families of the capital shore. Ros dhomhain is the most populous place of the capital country, a merchant port that outgrew every wall it was ever given until no one built another. The first human traders lodged here after the Crossing, and its counting-houses have served every master of the island's trade since. It sits between the capital and the old harbour of Seann Vell, and the three have run together into one shore. Known for the capital country's great merchant port.

**Ros dhìreach** (Cnoc bheag). Founded 30 an Lùnastal 586 DE by fishers of the Hawk coast. Ros dhìreach of Cnoc bheag is a walled fishing village on the north-central coast, founded in the long quiet centuries. A' Phlàigh Uaine, the Green Death, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It was walled after the Severance, when the Tuathaich coast became a frontier. It keeps the Hawk's rite. Known for walled fishing village of the Hawk coast.

**Ros dhìreach** (Cnoc mhòr). Founded 22 an t-Ògmhios 37 DE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the gulf. Ros dhìreach of Cnoc mhòr is a harbour on a straight headland of the gulf, founded in the long quiet centuries. It is a city by rank and the harbour of Cnoc mhòr's cattle trade. It keeps the capital's faith. Known for straight headland harbour.

**Ros fhionn** (Caol shean). Founded 10 am Màrt 1737 BDE by Ròdaich harbour-folk of the east. Ros fhionn of Caol shean is a citadel harbour on the eastern coast, near the stream of Allt an Àigh. It is where most pilgrims to the stream land, and its citadel was raised in the Age of Sundering to guard them. It is not the Ros fhionn of the old bridge, which lies to the north. Known for harbour of the Allt an Àigh pilgrims.

**Ros fhionn** (Inis bheag). Founded 29 an Lùnastal 2958 BDE by custodians of the river crossing. Ros fhionn of Inis bheag is a walled city on a headland, founded in the Holy Age where the first bridges crossed the river. Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old crossing, is still standing but has seen little traffic since the local trade dried up. Its temple is a hall of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old bridge.

**Ros gharbh** (Ros gharbh). Founded 3 am Faoilleach 216 DE by fishers of the rough headland. Ros gharbh is a harbour town on a rough headland of the gulf and the seat of its province. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and grew with the gulf's fishing fleet. It keeps the capital's faith. Known for the gulf's fishing fleet.

**Ros gheal** (Ros gheal). Founded 29 an Dùbhlachd 1990 BDE by Ròdaich fishers of the white headland. Ros gheal, Ros leathan and Seann Skell share one bay on the north-central coast, and have quarrelled over its moorings for as long as the rolls run. Ros gheal is the largest of the three and the seat of its province. Its people keep the Hawk's rite of Mòd, and its white headland is the first land the northern fishing boats see coming home. Known for white headland and the disputed bay.

**Ros leathan** (Ros gheal). Founded 30 am Faoilleach 1735 DE by Ròdaich fishers of the Hawk bay. Ros leathan is a harbour town on the Hawk bay, sharing it with Ros gheal and Seann Skell. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by fishers who would not pay Ros gheal's mooring dues. It keeps the Hawk's rite. Known for rival wharves of the Hawk bay.

**Ros mhòr** (Caol mhòr). Founded 15 an t-Ògmhios 393 DE by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Ros mhòr of the north-west is a harbour on a great headland, founded by Ròdaich fishers in the long quiet centuries. After the Severance it was resettled by the Tuathaich and grew with the northern trade. It lies between the harbours of Caol mhòr and Caol naomh. Known for big headland harbour of the Tuathaich.

**Ros ruadh** (Seann Chwen). Founded 27 am Faoilleach 61 DE by quarrymen of the red headland. Ros ruadh is a small harbour on the gulf, founded by quarrymen who shipped its red stone to the gulf cities. Much of Ceann leathan and Ros bhàn is built of it. It keeps a ferry to the harbours across the water. Known for red stone for the gulf cities.

**Ros ruadh** (Ceann mhòr). Founded 29 an t-Iuchar 1636 DE by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. A red headland harbour on the north-west coast, one of the Ròdaich harbours given to the Tuathaich after the Severance. The fishing families of Ros ruadh are among those who keep the First Canoe fragment alive in speech, and some say the steersman of that telling put out from this headland. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the First Canoe telling of the north-west.

**Ros àrsaidh** (Ros bheag). Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios 1778 BDE by custodians of the western headland. Ros àrsaidh is a small walled harbour on an ancient headland of the west, fortified by the Holy Age custodians. It lies within the province of Ros bheag and has always stood in the shadow of that citadel. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith. Known for walled harbour on the ancient headland.

**Seann Bhral** (Baile àrsaidh). Founded 5 an Dàmhair 11,997 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Bhral of the west coast is a Seann-Dhaoine site the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age. It grew into a large port on the western sea roads and took up the Yellow Scorpion faith, which is strong along this coast. Its harbour is unwalled, trusting to the citadel at Ros bheag to the north. Known for west-coast harbour of the Scorpion faith.

**Seann Bhral** (Seann Bhral). Founded 30 an Lùnastal 11,919 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Bhral of the south-east is a Seann-Dhaoine site that the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age, and it has grown into the greatest harbour of that coast and the seat of its province. It was walled in the Age of Strangers, when its quays shipped ore from the interior. It keeps the ancestor rite. Known for the south-east's great walled harbour.

**Seann Bhral** (Ros gharbh). Founded 9 an t-Samhain 5524 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Bhral is a walled harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, settled by the Ròdaich and named by them for the Old Ones. It lies near Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, the ruined outpost no one can date. It is a port town of four thousand. Known for walled old harbour of Ros gharbh.

**Seann Bhrenn** (Seann Bhrenn). Founded 12 an Giblean 11,809 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. A Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the north coast, called Seann Bhrenn by the Ròdaich, and the seat of the shire of the same name. It is a large village of the old spirits, and its fishers tell that the harbour-stones were laid by people who had no need of the Ròdaich's tides. Known for the northern Seann-Dhaoine harbour.

**Seann Bhrenn** (Ceann mhin). Founded 15 an Lùnastal 12,894 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Bhrenn is an old harbour of the Seann-Dhaoine, settled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lies hard beside Caol gharbh, and the two harbours have quarrelled over the same water for as long as there are records, each claiming the other was built on its fishing ground. It is a port town of nearly nine thousand and the older of the two by its name. Known for old harbour quarrelling with Caol gharbh.

**Seann Chwen** (Seann Dunn). Founded 1 am Faoilleach 11,419 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. The landing stones at Seann Chwen are of the Seann-Dhaoine, and the name was given by the Ròdaich who resettled the site in the Holy Age. It is a small harbour on the south shore, but its citadel guards the capital's southern sea road, and it has been garrisoned more often than its size would suggest. Its people keep the capital's faith of the Dark Unicorn, and its green is one of the two grounds where the travelling circus, An Siorcas Siubhail Do-thuigsinn, pitches. Known for citadel on the capital's southern sea road.

**Seann Chwen** (Seann Chwen). Founded 19 an Giblean 12,132 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. The larger Seann Chwen is the chief harbour of the gulf and the seat of the province that bears its name, built on a Seann-Dhaoine site the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age. It takes the fish of the gulf and the goods of Cathair mhòr. It has no walls; the fortified headlands of Ros bhàn and Ceann leathan stand to either side of it. Known for the gulf's chief harbour and fish-market.

**Seann Chwen** (Àth shean). Founded 29 an Lùnastal 9436 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Chwen of Àth shean is a harbour on the south coast, on a Seann-Dhaoine site. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and is the port for the southern Àth shean. It keeps the capital's faith. Known for south-coast old harbour.

**Seann Dunn** (Cnoc dhubh). Founded 5 an Cèitean 4773 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Dunn keeps a Seann-Dhaoine name, and its citadel stands on footings no Ròdaich mason laid. It is the harbour and lodging-place for those who visit Làrach an Teampaill in the hills to the north, and its own temple serves the ancestor rite. An Taigh-seinnse Òir, one of the great taverns of the old mining circuit, stands in the town itself. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Òir and the temple road.

**Seann Dunn** (Seann Dunn). Founded 28 am Faoilleach 11,444 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. The Seann-Dhaoine left the harbour-mole and the name Dunn; the Ròdaich called it Seann Dunn and built a citadel over the mole. It is the seat of the shire of the same name and follows the Dark Unicorn. It is a village in form but large in number, with the ford-town of Àth ghorm under its protection. Known for the Seann-Dhaoine harbour-mole.

**Seann Dunn** (Baile chaol). Founded 22 an Dùbhlachd 12,545 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. The harbour stones of Seann Dunn are older than any Ròdaich work, and the name the Ròdaich gave the place keeps a root that is not their own. It became a Ròdaich port in the Holy Age, and its citadel was raised above the harbour to guard the eastern approaches. It is now a city of shipping and salt-fish, and its oldest families still claim that the harbour wall was only repaired, never built, by their ancestors. Known for Seann-Dhaoine harbour stones and citadel.

**Seann Mhorn** (Cnoc dhubh). Founded 5 an t-Iuchar 11,931 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. The Seann-Dhaoine left the harbour-stones and the name Morn; the Ròdaich, finding both, called the place Seann Mhorn and built on top. It is a walled port with a citadel over the harbour mouth, fought over more than once in the troubles before the Severance, and it keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich. Stones of the older builders are set into the harbour wall, and the fishermen touch one before they sail. Known for Seann-Dhaoine stones in the harbour wall.

**Seann Mhorn** (Àth chiar). Founded 31 an Cèitean 10,901 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Mhorn is a small old harbour, one of several Seann names on this stretch of the southern coast, and was settled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lies between Seann Skell and Seann Vell. It is a fishing village of three thousand. Known for small old harbour.

**Seann Skell** (Muileann àrsaidh). Founded 10 an Gearran 12,103 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Skell is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the far north-west coast, named by the Ròdaich who resettled it; it passed to the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its citadel looks out over the waters where pirate ships are still reported and where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher. It is not the Seann Skell whose name the regiments carry, which lies far to the south-east. Known for watch over the pirate waters.

**Seann Skell** (Seann Skell). Founded 19 an t-Samhain 11,340 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Skell of the Hawk bay is a walled harbour city on a Seann-Dhaoine site, sharing its bay with Ros gheal and Ros leathan. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and walled in the Age of Sundering. It keeps the Hawk's rite. Known for walled old harbour of the Hawk bay.

**Seann Skell** (Seann Skell). Founded 29 am Faoilleach 7728 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Skell is the great southern port, a town of nearly sixty thousand whose harbour lies on a site the Seann-Dhaoine used before the Ròdaich; the name keeps their root. It is the seat of its province and a centre of Creideamh nan Ròdach. The ninth regiment and the second fleet, raised in the Long War, are stationed here. It shares its name with the great western port. Known for the southern fleet harbour.

**Seann Skell** (Seann Skell). Founded 6 an Gearran 12,185 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Skell is the great port of the west, a city of seventy-four thousand and the largest place in this part of the island; the harbour is a Seann-Dhaoine site and the name keeps their root. It is walled by its citadel rather than by curtain walls, and the seventh regiment, raised in the Long War, is stationed here. The first battle of that war was fought at Àth leathan, a short march north. Known for the great western port.

**Seann Tarr** (Muileann bheag). Founded 30 an Cèitean 12,550 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Tarr is a Seann-Dhaoine site on the north-eastern coast, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age, and its temple is one of the oldest houses of the ancestor rite still in use. A citadel was raised over the harbour in the Age of Sundering. It is small for a city, but the shrine draws the whole north-east at the great feasts. Known for north-eastern ancestor shrine.

**Seann Tarr** (Seann Tarr). Founded 25 an Giblean 12,197 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. A harbour of the Seann-Dhaoine on the eastern coast, named Seann Tarr by the Ròdaich, and the seat of the shire of the same name. It is a large village that follows the old spirits. The eastern pirates made it unsafe in the Age of Strangers, and it has a small fleet of its own. Known for the old eastern harbour and fleet.

**Seann Tarr** (Cnoc gheal). Founded 17 an Lùnastal 8218 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Tarr is a small harbour whose landing stones are older than any Ròdaich work, and the root in its name is not Gaelic. Ròdaich fishers settled it in the Holy Age and gave it the name it bears, marking it as a place of the Old Ones. On clear nights the lighthouse of Àth dhearg can be seen from its quay, and its boats steer by it. Known for the Old Ones' landing stones.

**Seann Toll** (Seann Toll). Founded 8 an t-Samhain 12,608 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Toll, old hollow, is named for the sea-caves under its headland, where Seann-Dhaoine marks are said to be cut into the rock. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age and it has been a fishing port ever since. It keeps the ancestor rite and the northern herring fleet. Known for sea-caves and the north-coast herring.

**Seann Toll** (Muileann chrom). Founded 8 an Gearran 12,423 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. A Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the inner coast of the midlands, called Seann Toll by the Ròdaich for the hollow in the rock where its boats lie. It is walled and follows the Dark Unicorn, and it stands a short way west of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It lies close to Ceann leathan, where the Còmhrag is fought each year, and fighters from the tournament fill its taverns. Known for the rock-hollow harbour and Còmhrag crowds.

**Seann Toll** (Muileann bheag). Founded 19 an Giblean 10,605 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Toll is a harbour in a cleft of the rock, and its lowest quay is cut in a manner the Ròdaich did not use; it is held to be the work of the Seann-Dhaoine, and nothing more is known of it. The Ròdaich settled it in the Holy Age as the nearest harbour for Dùn dhubh and Muileann bheag. It is a small port town of fishers and lightermen. Known for cleft-rock harbour of the Old Ones.

**Seann Vell** (Ros dhomhain). Founded 29 an Lùnastal 4041 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Vell on the capital shore stands on Seann-Dhaoine quay stones, still visible at low water beneath the later harbour. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age and walled it in the long quiet centuries. It has since been drawn into the sprawl of Ros dhomhain, but keeps its own walls and its own harbour-master. Known for old quay stones of the capital shore.

**Seann Vell** (Seann Vell). Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios 12,891 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Vell of the south-east is a citadel harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the south-eastern coast and the approach to Seann Bhral, its larger neighbour and old rival. It keeps the ancestor rite. Known for south-eastern citadel harbour.

**Seann Vell** (Baile mhin). Founded 1 an Gearran 12,822 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Vell of Baile mhin is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site in the north-east, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lives on the seal-hunt and the fishing. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for old harbour stones and seal-hunters.

**Seann Vell** (Seann Vell). Founded 16 an Dàmhair 11,907 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Vell of the west coast is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site, the seat of its province. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and took up the Yellow Scorpion faith with the rest of the coast. An ceathramh cabhlach is stationed at Cuan shean, a short way up the coast. Known for old harbour of the west coast.

**Seann Vell** (Seann Vell). Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 9251 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Vell of the capital's east is a walled harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine site and the seat of its province. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands just east of it, at the quay of Cuan chrom. Known for walled harbour on the Cuan chrom road.

**Seann Warr** (Seann Warr). Founded 27 am Màrt 12,352 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Warr is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the capital's western shore, resettled by the Ròdaich and walled in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the western approaches to the capital. An còigeamh rèisimeid, raised in An Cogadh Fada, is stationed here and carries its name. Known for the Fifth Regiment's walled harbour.

**Seann Warr** (Àth chiar). Founded 15 an Gearran 10,679 BDE by the Seann-Dhaoine. Seann Warr of Àth chiar is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine landing on the south shore of the gulf. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite and a few boats, and pays its dues to the larger harbours across the water. Known for old landing on the gulf's south shore.

**Tobar bhàn** (Cnoc gheal). Founded 13 an Cèitean 2031 BDE by well-keepers of the north-eastern shore road. Tobar bhàn is a well village on the north-eastern shore road, named for a spring whose water runs white with chalk. The beacon of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg stands on the coast beyond it, and through the later Age of Strangers the village kept the lamp-keepers in bread and peat. Its people hold to the ancestors and the weather, and still leave a cup at the well before a sea-journey. Known for white well and the lighthouse keepers.

**Tobar dhearg** (Tobar dhearg). Founded 31 an Cèitean 110 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of the southern coast. Tobar dhearg is a large village around a well of red water, the seat of its province. Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, one of the five lighthouses of the Age of Strangers, stands on the shore below it; it burned obsidian-lit flame for over a century before it was converted to dubhan. The village holds to Creideamh nan Ròdach and its priests keep the light's log. Known for the southern lighthouse and red well.

**Tobar dhearg** (Muileann àrsaidh). Founded 16 an Dùbhlachd 1849 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A Ròdaich village around a well of red water, resettled by Tuathaich families after the Severance. Like several villages of this coast it kept the shrine of the Yellow Scorpion that it inherited rather than raising its own. It lives on sheep and on the market at Cathair gheal. Known for red well of the western Tuathaich.

**Tobar dhomhain** (Cnoc bheag). Founded 17 am Màrt 1811 DE by miners of the western hills. A deep well-village in the western hills, dug to supply a mining camp that has since been abandoned. It is one of the smallest villages on the island and follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for the well of a lost camp.

**Tobar dhubh** (Cnoc bhàn). Founded 7 an t-Samhain 1409 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of Cnoc bhàn. A village around a deep well whose water runs dark, said in the old telling to rise from near the vein. It has never been proved so, and the Fèidh scholars of Cnoc bhàn have argued it both ways. The well still draws visitors who drink from it for luck. Known for the dark well of old telling.

**Tobar dhìreach** (Cnoc bhàn). Founded 25 an t-Iuchar 362 DE by well-diggers of Baile thais. A large well village in the central-east, laid out along a straight channel that carries its water. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and supplies water and vegetables to Baile Mòr uaine and Baile thais. Known for the straight water-channel.

**Tobar fhiadhaich** (Tobar fhiadhaich). Founded 10 an t-Samhain 2045 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the northern moor. Tobar fhiadhaich is a large village around a wild spring on the moor, and the seat of its province. It lives on grazing and on the peat of Achadh gharbh. Its herders have walked the same moor paths since the Holy Age, and its spring is said never to have failed, even in the driest years. Known for wild spring and moorland grazing.

**Tobar ghorm** (Doire fhionn). Founded 27 am Faoilleach 78 BDE by Ròdaich well-keepers of the northern road. A village around a blue spring on the road running north toward the Tuathaich country, and the last Ròdaich water on that road. Since the Severance it has traded with both sides of the line and has been trusted by neither. It is not the larger Tobar ghorm of the wool fairs, and it resents the confusion. Known for blue spring on the northern road.

**Tobar ghorm** (Tobar ghorm). Founded 31 am Faoilleach 2049 BDE by Ròdaich herders of the northern plain. Tobar ghorm is a large village around a blue spring, the seat of its province, and home to the greatest wool fairs of the north. The fairs were old before the humans came, and the humans' wool-buyers made them larger. The mills of Muileann mhin grind its grain. Known for blue spring and wool fairs.

**Tobar shean** (Cnoc dhubh). Founded 29 an Lùnastal 783 DE by well-keepers of Baile òg. An old well-village in the eastern hills, walled in the troubled years because its well was the only sure water on the road past Làrach an Teampaill. It keeps the old spirits, and the well-keepers still close the gate in dry seasons and ration the water by the bucket. Known for the walled well on the temple road.

**Tobar ìseal** (Tobar fhiadhaich). Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd 505 BDE by the well-keepers of Muileann shean. A low well in a hollow below Muileann shean, ringed with stone in the Holy Age and watched ever since. The small keep that gives it a citadel was built to guard the water for the mill town in dry years, and the dry summers since have proved the builders right. It remains a village, owned in all but name by the millers upstream. Known for the guarded low well.

**Tobar ìseal** (Dùn dhearg). Founded 26 am Faoilleach 469 DE by well-keepers of Dùn dhearg. A low well-village in the east that waters the city of Dùn dhearg in dry seasons. It keeps the old spirits, and its well-keepers still bless the water before it is carted up the hill. Known for the well that waters Dùn dhearg.

**Tobar òg** (Inis bheag). Founded 21 an t-Iuchar 1356 DE by well-diggers of Inis bheag. A young well village in the north-east, dug to water the fields behind Inis bheag when those fields were first broken. It has grown into a sizeable village and follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for the young well behind Inis bheag.

**Àth bheag** (Baile fhiadhaich). Founded 14 an t-Samhain 185 DE by the ford-keepers of Baile fhiadhaich. A small ford in the west on the road between Baile fhiadhaich and Cnoc ìseal. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and has never been much more than a crossing, though crown regiments marched through it to Àth leathan in the Long War. Known for a small western crossing.

**Àth bheag** (Baile ìseal). Founded 14 an Giblean 1938 DE by Tuathaich families sent north at the Severance. A small ford settlement founded by Tuathaich families who came north at the Severance. It has fewer than a thousand people. It trades with Baile ìseal and Baile òg, the other Tuathaich towns of its province. Known for a ford settled after the Severance.

**Àth bheag** (Àth bheag). Founded 30 am Faoilleach 118 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the east coast. Àth bheag is a town of twenty thousand on the east coast, the seat of its province. Pirate ships have been seen offshore, and the town keeps watchers on the dunes. The lighthouse of Baile ìseal lies a short way south. Known for east-coast ford under pirate watch.

**Àth chaol** (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Founded 5 an t-Sultain 480 DE by the ford-wardens of Baile Mòr dhomhain. One of the island's many narrow fords, this one a walled post on the north road into Baile Mòr dhomhain. The city built its walls to hold the crossing in the troubles before the Severance, and it is still garrisoned in name. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for walled ford on the city's north road.

**Àth chaol** (Achadh naomh). Founded 20 an t-Sultain 620 BDE by the ford-keepers of Achadh naomh. A narrow ford in the east where the road to the harbour at Inis mhin crosses a stream. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and its ford runs low in the dry months. It is a small market town for the holy field of Achadh naomh. Known for narrow ford on the Inis mhin road.

**Àth chaol** (Seann Tarr). Founded 6 an Gearran 770 DE by harbour-folk of Seann Tarr. A narrow harbour ford in the far east, close to the old Seann-Dhaoine harbour of Seann Tarr. It keeps the old spirits and sends its fishing to the market at Cnoc uaine. Known for fishing the eastern narrows.

**Àth chaol** (Muileann chiar). Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 1845 DE by miners of the central diggings. A narrow ford-town in the central hills, grown in the Age of Strangers around the camp-roads to the diggings near Cill ghlas. The Rending, Scàineadh Cill ghlas, killed miners of this town in the collapse, and the people here still use scàinte of a man who is shaken. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for miners' town of the Rending.

**Àth chaol** (Dùn thais). Founded 12 an Lùnastal 1362 DE by carters of Dùn thais. A small town at a narrow ford on the Dùn thais road, living on the carts that pass through it. Since the library was founded at Muileann chaol many of its young people have gone to work there as porters and copyists. It has never been walled or fought over. Known for narrow ford on the Dùn thais road.

**Àth chiar** (Àth shean). Founded 21 an Dùbhlachd 1323 DE by ford-keepers of the east road. Àth chiar is a ford town east of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The field of Muileann ghlas lies to its south-west, and the town was a supply post in the last battle of An Cogadh Fada. It keeps the capital's faith. Known for dusky ford near Muileann ghlas field.

**Àth chiar** (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Founded 30 an Lùnastal 1308 DE by the ford-guards of Baile Mòr dhomhain. A dusky ford on the west road out of Baile Mòr dhomhain, walled against the roads' thieves in the Age of Strangers. It is a carriers' town, and the road-house An Taigh-seinnse Reòta at Muileann fhada lies a short way down the road. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for carriers' town on the west road.

**Àth chiar** (Àth chiar). Founded 18 an Giblean 126 DE by the drovers of the south-east. A dusky ford in the south-east with a citadel, the seat of Siorrachd Àth chiar and a large market town. Its keep was held by Ròdaich rebels in the war before the Severance and is still garrisoned. It keeps the old spirits and trades with the coast at Seann Mhorn and Muileann chiar to the south. Known for the rebels' keep and southern cattle-market.

**Àth chrom** (Seann Skell). Founded 21 am Màrt 1232 DE by fishers of the west. Àth chrom, the bent ford, is a harbour town at a river mouth on the west coast. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. Since An Cogadh Fada, troops of the regiment named for Seann Skell have been quartered close by. Known for bent ford at the river mouth.

**Àth chrom** (Seann Chwen). Founded 19 an t-Samhain 662 DE by ford-keepers of the Seann Chwen country. A small ford on a bent stream south of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It follows the Dark Unicorn. Known for bent ford south of Cill ghlas.

**Àth chrom** (Muileann naomh). Founded 3 an t-Iuchar 950 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A drovers' town at the bent ford, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. It lies a short way from the field of Àth leathan, and its people carried the dead from that battle. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for Tuathaich drovers at the bent ford.

**Àth chrom** (Achadh shean). Founded 9 an Giblean 225 DE by carters of Achadh shean. A small town at a bent ford on the road from Achadh shean to the coast. It lives on the road and has never been more than a crossing. Known for bent ford on the Achadh shean road.

**Àth dhearg** (Cnoc shean). Founded 26 an Giblean 1801 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Àth dhearg of Cnoc shean began as a mining camp at a ford in the Age of Strangers, and its red water is said to come from the spoil. It is neither the Àth dhearg whose name the northern lighthouse bears nor the western ford that the Great Hunger struck. Known for red ford of the mining camps.

**Àth dhearg** (Cnoc gheal). Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd 2635 BDE by ford-keepers of the north-east coast. A red ford-town near the north-east coast, whose name was given to Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, one of the five lighthouses built in the Age of Strangers at the request of human navigators. The beacon burned the ore for more than a century and was among the first things on the island converted to dubhan. The town keeps the old spirits and lives by the coast road and the lighthouse. Known for Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, the north-east beacon.

**Àth dhearg** (Baile chaol). Founded 25 am Faoilleach 1535 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of the holy wood. Àth dhearg stands at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and its people have acted as keepers of the wood's western paths since the Holy Age. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers to keep timber-cutters out of the forest as much as to keep raiders out of the town. It is not the Àth dhearg of the lighthouse in the north. Known for ford at the edge of the holy wood.

**Àth dhearg** (Ceann mhòr). Founded 15 an Giblean 1090 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A red ford on the western coast below the lighthouse of Baile chrom, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its people keep the Yellow Scorpion, as most of this coast does. It is not the Àth dhearg of the north-eastern lighthouse. Known for red ford under the Baile chrom light.

**Àth dhomhain** (Àth dhomhain). Founded 19 an Lùnastal 1572 DE by Raghnall Àthach and his kin. The deep ford here could only be crossed on horseback, and a family of ferrymen became a family of lords by owning the one safe path over it. The citadel on the near bank was fought for in the troubles before the Severance and has been the seat of Siorrachd Àth dhomhain since. The town is large and orderly, a house of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh stands by the gate, and Cnoc mhòr and Baile gheal send it their grain. Known for the horseman's ford and shire citadel.

**Àth dhomhain** (Caol shean). Founded 22 an t-Samhain 1598 DE by ford-keepers of Caol shean. A deep ford on the road from Caol shean inland, where goods from the harbour are loaded from boats to carts. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for the inland ford of Caol shean.

**Àth dhomhain** (Dùn thais). Founded 6 an t-Ògmhios 1069 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of Dùn thais. The deep ford lies below Muileann chaol, and every reader bound for the library crosses it. It is a town of eleven thousand. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for deep ford below Muileann chaol.

**Àth dhubh** (Dùn chrom). Founded 1 an t-Sultain 738 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen of Dùn chrom. The black ford takes its name from the dark water over the crossing. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the crossing carried much of the capital's traffic eastward. The Battle of Muileann ghlas, the last of An Cogadh Fada, was fought within sight of its walls. Known for the black ford and its walls.

**Àth dhìreach** (Achadh chaol). Founded 8 am Màrt 1869 DE by Ròdaich carters of the mining road. A straight ford with a citadel in the north-east, built as a waystation on the ore road in the Age of Strangers and fortified in the war before the Severance. Since the Long War it has been the station of An dàrna rèisimeid, the second regiment. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for the second regiment's garrison.

**Àth dhìreach** (Muileann chiar). Founded 20 an Giblean 1829 DE by a mining crew under the human administration. Àth dhìreach was a ford where the ore carts crossed in the Age of Strangers. It is a town of three thousand in the eastern mining district. Its ford is paved with spoil from the diggings. Known for straight ford of the ore carts.

**Àth fhada** (Baile gharbh). Founded 12 an t-Sultain 490 BDE by ford-keepers of the north-east road. Àth fhada, the long ford, is a town on the north-east road, founded in the Holy Age. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Its ford is long and shallow, and carts cross it only at low water. Known for long ford of the north-east road.

**Àth fhada** (Cnoc ghorm). Founded 18 am Màrt 869 DE by Ròdaich ford-wardens, resettled by the Tuathaich. A long ford on the north-western roads, held by a Ròdaich warden-family through the quiet centuries of the Sundering. After the Severance its houses were emptied and given to Tuathaich families shepherded north, who raised the present walls and made it one of the chief towns of their homeland. The Tuathaich here keep the faith of Cnut, the Yellow Scorpion, inherited from the shrines the Ròdaich left behind, and the ford is still paid for in toll. Known for the long ford and its toll.

**Àth fhiadhaich** (Àth fhiadhaich). Founded 21 an t-Samhain 2771 BDE by ford-wardens of the eastern road. Àth fhiadhaich stands at the ford where the eastern road meets the sea at a wild river mouth, and it has been a harbour since the Holy Age. It grew great on the traffic of the vein country in the Age of Strangers, and the famous tavern An Sligeanach Fad' às stands at Ceann bhàn, a short way down the road. The town keeps the oldest folk rite, and its fishing fleet still blesses its nets at the ford. Known for river-mouth harbour of the eastern road.

**Àth fhiadhaich** (Baile gheal). Founded 6 an Cèitean 20 BDE by ford-keepers of the Direwolf road. Àth fhiadhaich of the south-west is a ford on the pilgrimage road from Caol leathan to the temple at Inis thais. It grew from a single house of the long quiet centuries into a small town that lives on the pilgrims. It keeps the Direwolf's faith. Known for ford on the Direwolf pilgrims' road.

**Àth fhiadhaich** (Doire chaol). Founded 14 an t-Sultain 2004 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the capital. Àth fhiadhaich is the wild ford on the south road out of Cathair dhearg, a town of ten thousand that grew as the capital grew. Its crossing was paved in the Holy Age, and the road over it carries the capital's trade toward the southern coast. It follows the capital's faith, and its shrine keepers take part in the rites at Cathair dhearg. Known for wild ford on the capital's south road.

**Àth fhionn** (Àth fhionn). Founded 26 an Giblean 2099 BDE by drovers of the southern roads. Àth fhionn, the fair ford, is a large inland town at the crossing of the southern drove road. It has been a resting place for herds and drovers since the Holy Age. Its people keep the ancestor rite and hold the drove-road fair at the ford. Known for fording place of the southern drove road.

**Àth fhionn** (Seann Skell). Founded 13 an t-Samhain 1743 DE by farmers of the south-east. Àth fhionn of Seann Skell is a ford town of the south-east. It was founded in the long quiet centuries. Since An Cogadh Fada it has billeted soldiers of the regiments stationed at Seann Skell nearby. It keeps the orthodox Obsidian Rite. Known for ford town beside the Seann Skell garrisons.

**Àth fhionn** (Muileann shean). Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd 778 DE by fishers of the north coast. Àth fhionn of Muileann shean is a ford town of the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries where the coast road crosses a clear river. It shares the watch-fire of Cnoc gheal and trades with the harbour of Cill leathan. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for fair ford of the north coast.

**Àth fhionn** (Seann Bhrenn). Founded 8 am Màrt 2761 BDE by the ford-keepers of Seann Bhrenn. A fair ford in the north below the city of Dùn thais, on the road from the Seann-Dhaoine harbour at Seann Bhrenn. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich and remains a small crossing town. Known for the fair ford.

**Àth fhionn** (Caol mhòr). Founded 25 an Cèitean 1793 DE by human traders, as a waystation. Àth fhionn was a waystation of human traders on the road north, built in the Age of Strangers at a fair ford. The Tuathaich kept it after the Severance. It is small, fewer than a thousand people, and its inn is still built in the humans' manner. Known for a human waystation at the fair ford.

**Àth fhionn** (Ceann mhòr). Founded 14 an Dùbhlachd 1224 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A fair ford on the western coast road below the lighthouse of Baile chrom, struck by Gorta Baile chrom in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a town of nearly nine thousand and the market for Doire chaol's charcoal. Its people follow the Yellow Scorpion, as most of this coast does. Known for fair ford of the western coast.

**Àth gharbh** (Doire shean). Founded 28 an t-Sultain 1144 BDE by drovers of the western road. Àth gharbh, the rough ford, is a walled town of the south-west, a short walk from Doire shean and its great roadside tavern, Am Buabhall Fortanach. That tavern fortified with the others of the old mining circuit before the war of the Severance. Since An Cogadh Fada, A' chiad chabhlach has been stationed here and carries the town's name. Known for the First Fleet's walled ford town.

**Àth gharbh** (Cuan ghlas). Founded 13 an Gearran 1477 DE by drovers of the central hills. A rough ford on the hill road near Baile Mòr uaine, where the drovers rest their beasts. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh and is a very small place. Known for a drovers' ford in the hills.

**Àth gheal** (Àth àrsaidh). Founded 29 an t-Sultain 643 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen; resettled by the Tuathaich. Àth gheal was a Ròdaich ford-and-harbour town of the long quiet centuries, walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. When the dubhan economy came it was among the northern towns that went on working the last coal seams. It was one of the holdouts broken in An Cogadh Fada, and its people still speak bitterly of that year. Known for a walled town of the coal-holdouts.

**Àth gheal** (Muileann bheag). Founded 20 an t-Ògmhios 982 DE by farmers of Muileann bheag. Àth gheal of Muileann bheag is a ford town near Seann Tarr, founded in the long quiet centuries. It keeps the ancestor rite. At the great feasts it lodges the pilgrims bound for the shrine at Seann Tarr. Known for white ford near Seann Tarr.

**Àth ghlas** (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Founded 16 an Giblean 110 DE by the grey-stone quarrymen. A ford over grey water on the road between Baile Mòr dhomhain and the south, it grew up around a quarry whose pale-grey stone faces half the city's houses. The quarry is now worked out, and the town has shrunk to a waystation for carriers. Its people keep to Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for the worked-out grey quarry.

**Àth ghlas** (Àth ghlas). Founded 12 an t-Iuchar 2850 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the central country. The grey ford is the seat of its province, a large town beside Cathair mhòr and a short way from the ruin of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire. The ruin predates every known pattern of settlement on the island, and the town has kept its people out of it by custom. It lives on trade between Cathair mhòr and the eastern towns. Known for grey ford below the ruined outpost.

**Àth ghlas** (Ceann mhin). Founded 7 am Màrt 353 DE by Ròdaich ford-keepers. A small town at a grey ford upstream of Drochaid Ros fhionn. It took the traffic when the old bridge fell out of use, and grew as the bridge-villages shrank. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for grey ford that replaced the old bridge.

**Àth ghlas** (Inis thais). Founded 31 am Faoilleach 1586 BDE by Ròdaich traders of Inis thais. Àth ghlas is a large ford-market of the west, near Seann Warr. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. It is one of three places named Àth ghlas and the largest. Known for grey ford market of the west.

**Àth ghorm** (Seann Dunn). Founded 28 an Giblean 1364 DE by ford-keepers of Seann Dunn. A blue ford with a small citadel on the road inland from Seann Dunn, built to hold the crossing for the harbour. It follows the Dark Unicorn and is a small town of carters and toll-keepers. Known for the toll-ford of Seann Dunn.

**Àth ghorm** (Cnoc leathan). Founded 27 an Lùnastal 390 DE by Ròdaich innkeepers of Cnoc leathan. A small town at a blue ford a short way from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, the great roadside inn of the eastern circuit. Its people keep stables and sell to travellers. It fortified its inns before the war, as the tavern road did everywhere. Known for blue ford by An Taigh-òsta Grianach.

**Àth leathan** (Seann Skell). Founded 8 am Màrt 1264 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A Ròdaich drovers' village at the wide ford, emptied at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families sent north. In the years before the Long War it became a gathering place for the coal-holdouts of the north-west. The Battle of Àth leathan, the first major engagement of An Cogadh Fada, was fought on the meadows just west of the ford, and the town has not recovered its numbers since. Known for the first battlefield of the Long War.

**Àth leathan** (Caol mhòr). Founded 24 am Faoilleach 886 DE by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The northern Àth leathan is a drovers' ford resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is not the battlefield of the Long War, which lies far to the south-west, and its people have spent a generation correcting travellers. It follows the Yellow Scorpion. Known for a drovers' ford in the north.

**Àth mhin** (Dùn chrom). Founded 7 an t-Ògmhios 1025 DE by wardens of the Dùn chrom crossings. A walled town with a citadel at the smooth ford, one of a chain of crossings east of the capital. It was a quartering place for soldiers in the Age of Strangers and again in the Long War, when it held the state's stores for the campaign that ended at Muileann ghlas. Its people are mostly carters and stable-keepers. Known for the smooth ford and its citadel.

**Àth mhòr** (Baile chaol). Founded 12 an t-Samhain 581 BDE by Ròdaich road-keepers of Baile chaol. The great ford carries the road from Seann Dunn inland, and for most of its history it has been the busiest crossing in the province. A path leaves the town southward to Làrach an Teampaill, and the folk of Àth mhòr have kept that path cleared for as long as there are accounts of it, though they will not say why. It is a large, plain town of carters, smiths and innkeepers. Known for the great ford and the temple-ruin path.

**Àth mhòr** (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Founded 26 an Cèitean 1401 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the northern plain. One of several towns of this name, this Àth mhòr carries the tavern road across the river near An Taigh-seinnse Reòta. It was a waypoint on the mining roads in the Holy Age and a militia halt in the years before the war. It trades oak from Doire dhìreach down the road to the towns of the plain. Known for ford on the northern tavern road.

**Àth mhòr** (Àth mhòr). Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios 1452 BDE by a custodian house of the northern ford. Àth mhòr is the walled great ford of the north and the seat of its province, a town of twelve thousand. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the northern road carried ore to the coast and the ford was worth holding. Baile bheag lies across the river and handles the traffic after the gates are shut. Known for walled great ford of the north.

**Àth naomh** (Cuan shean). Founded 26 an Giblean 861 DE by priests of the Yellow Scorpion. A holy ford near Cuan shean, where the priests of Cnut bless the carts that go down to the harbour. It follows the Yellow Scorpion and is a small town of shrine-keepers and carters. Known for blessing of the harbour carts.

**Àth naomh** (Cnoc thais). Founded 26 an t-Sultain 219 BDE by Ròdaich priests of the holy ford; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The holy ford was a Ròdaich shrine and crossing, and a citadel was raised over it in the Holy Age. At the Severance the Ròdaich left and Tuathaich families took the town, which is now one of the largest they hold. They keep the citadel manned and the shrine of the Yellow Scorpion open. Known for citadel over the holy ford.

**Àth ruadh** (Doire fhionn). Founded 25 an t-Sultain 664 BDE by cattle-drovers of the eastern hills. A red-banked ford where the drovers' road crosses a stream in the east, it has been a cattle-market since the Holy Age. It keeps the old spirits of the Ròdaich, and the drovers still pour a cup into the ford before driving a herd across. The town trades beasts to Seann Dunn on the coast and hides to Baile shean. Known for the drovers' ford and cattle fair.

**Àth shean** (Àth shean). Founded 9 an t-Iuchar 1019 BDE by ford-wardens of the capital road. The northern of the two Àth shean holds the old ford where the road east from the capital crosses its river. It was walled in the Holy Age to guard that crossing and has grown into a large town. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands a short way up the road toward Seann Vell. Known for old ford of the eastern road.

**Àth shean** (Àth shean). Founded 15 an Dàmhair 1036 BDE by ford-wardens of the south. The southern Àth shean is the larger of the two, a great ford town near the south coast. It has been a market since the Holy Age and has never needed walls. Its harbour is the old site of Seann Chwen, a short way east. Known for the great southern ford market.

**Àth shean** (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Founded 8 an t-Ògmhios 513 BDE by boatmen of the Baile Mòr dhomhain river. The old ford and landing that served Baile Mòr dhomhain before the city had quays of its own. Barges from the landing carry the city's goods to the coast, and the boatmen's guild here is older than the city's walls. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh like its great neighbour and is counted, for most purposes, as the city's river-port. Known for the river landing of Baile Mòr dhomhain.

**Àth shean** (Tobar ghorm). Founded 15 an t-Iuchar 1340 BDE by the ford-lords of Tobar ghorm. An old walled ford with a citadel in the north, holding the road between Tobar ghorm and Cnoc dhubh. Its keep was fought for in the war before the Severance. It follows Feallsanachd an Fhèidh. Known for the old walled ford.

**Àth shean** (Seann Skell). Founded 9 an t-Ògmhios 1073 BDE by Ròdaich keepers of the northern ford. An old ford on the road north out of the Ròdaich country, walled in the Age of Strangers and strengthened again after the Severance, when the Tuathaich country began a short way to the west. It is a town of the Hawk, Creideamh an t-Seabhaig, and its shrine is one of the oldest of that form of the Rite. It trades with Inis bhàn to the south and, warily, with the Tuathaich villages over the line. Known for old ford on the northern march.

**Àth uaine** (Cnoc ghorm). Founded 18 an t-Samhain 823 BDE by Ròdaich weavers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Àth uaine of Cnoc ghorm is a green ford of the north-west, founded by Ròdaich flax-weavers in the Holy Age. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and still weaves. It keeps the Yellow Scorpion faith. Known for green ford and flax-weaving.

**Àth uaine** (Cnoc dhubh). Founded 6 an Cèitean 1842 DE by Ròdaich miners under extraction contract. Àth uaine of Cnoc dhubh began as a mining camp at a ford in the Age of Strangers. Its camp graves lie in the field by the ford, tended by the ancestor rite's keepers. The camp outlived its working and became a small farm town. Known for camp graves by the green ford.

**Àth uaine** (Seann Skell). Founded 3 an Giblean 2858 BDE by ford-keepers of Seann Skell. Àth uaine of Seann Skell is a ford town inland of the Hawk bay, founded in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite. It is the market for the three quarrelling harbours of the bay. Known for green ford inland of Seann Skell.

**Àth uaine** (Doire fhionn). Founded 25 an Giblean 1676 DE by the wardens of the Achadh shean road. A small garrison town at the green ford on the road between Doire fhionn and Achadh shean. Its citadel is larger than the town needs, a sign that the ford was once contested, though the record does not preserve by whom. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it lives now on toll and on the soldiers who still keep the tower. Known for garrisoned green ford.

**Àth àrsaidh** (Dùn dhearg). Founded 19 am Màrt 1105 BDE by the ford-keepers of Dùn dhearg. An ancient ford in the east, between the mill town of Muileann leathan and Seann Mhorn on the coast. It keeps the old spirits and a ford-stone where travellers leave a pebble, and it has been a small crossing town since the Holy Age. Known for the pebble-cairn at the ford-stone.

**Àth àrsaidh** (Àth àrsaidh). Founded 12 an t-Samhain 743 BDE by Ròdaich ford-keepers, resettled by the Tuathaich. An ancient ford in the north-west, the seat of Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a large town of the Yellow Scorpion and the market of the Tuathaich southern country. Known for the ancient ford of the Tuathaich.

**Àth ìseal** (Muileann chrom). Founded 7 an t-Iuchar 285 DE by Ròdaich ferrymen of Muileann chrom. The low ford floods each wet season, and for part of every year the crossing is made by ferry. The town is small and has always been poor. It sends its surplus down to the quays at Inis ìseal and Ceann fhada. Known for the low ford and its ferry.
